results.claim: T9: liminf_n (p_{n+m}-p_n) < infinity for every m; H_1 <= 600; H_1 <= 12 under Elliott-Halberstam; prime k-tuples conjecture for a positive proportion of admissible k-tuples. Cited as J. Maynard, arXiv:1311.4600, Ann. of Math. 181 (2015) 383-413, volume/pages flagged 'not independently confirmed'.
results.paper_quote: Theorem 1.3: liminf_n(p_{n+1}-p_n) <= 600. Theorem 1.4: Assume that the primes have level of distribution theta for every theta < 1. Then liminf_n(p_{n+1}-p_n) <= 12, liminf_n(p_{n+2}-p_n) <= 600. Theorem 1.1: Let m in N. We have liminf_n(p_{n+m}-p_n) << m^3 e^{4m}. Theorem 1.2: ... #{ {h_1,...,h_m} subset A : for infinitely many n all of n+h_1,...,n+h_m are prime } / #{ {h_1,...,h_m} subset A } >>_m 1.
results.doc_quote: T9 -- `liminf_n (p_{n+m}-p_n) < inf` for every `m`; `H_1 <= 600`; `<= 12` under Elliott-Halberstam; prime `k`-tuples conjecture for a positive proportion of admissible `k`-tuples.
results.notes: Read the full HTML (arxiv.org/html/1311.4600v3, v3 of 28 Oct 2019) plus the abs page; the HTML fetch truncated in section 4, but section 1 carries every cited result under exactly the archive's numbering (Theorems 1.1-1.4). All four clauses match: 600 hangs on Thm 1.3 unconditionally, the <=12 is correctly conditional on level of distribution theta<1 (Thm 1.4), <infinity for every m is Thm 1.1, and the positive-proportion clause is the paper's own abstract wording. No dropped hypothesis or added uniformity; H_m is stated with no bound, as the document says. Journal ref 181 (2015) 383-413 is correct and flagged unconfirmed. v1 could not be diffed; v3 is a typo-fix revision.
